title: Water Transport in Plants
keyIdea: Water enters at the roots, travels up thin tubes in the stem, and reaches the leaves. A blocked stem stops the path so leaves above dry out — the celery-dye model makes the pathway visible.
familyTip: Stand a pale celery stick in coloured water. After a few hours, cut the stem and look for coloured tubes. Ask: where did the water travel?

visual.caption: Water-transport idea or mix-up? Drag each clue, or tap it then a box.

items: leaves drink soil with no stem path
flowers are the start of the water path
dye in celery shows the upward path

lab.caption: Flagship lab: roots drink, stem tubes rise, water reaches leaves, block the stem, order the path, catch leaf-drinks-soil myth.

kid: Water gets into a plant through the roots in the soil.
Thin tubes inside the stem carry that water up toward the leaves.
When water reaches the leaves, they can use it to make food.
If the stem is blocked, water cannot pass and the leaves above dry out.
adult: NC Y3 Plants: investigate the way in which water is transported within plants. The celery-in-dye demonstration shows coloured pathways in the stem. Distinct from How Plant Parts Work (jobs of roots/stem/leaves/flower) and Plants need water and light.

Words: transport, roots, stem tubes (xylem), pathway, block. Common mistakes: thinking leaves drink soil water with no stem path; starting the path at the flower; ignoring that a crush/block stops flow above that point.
In the lab your child shows roots drinking, opens stem tubes, sends water to leaves, blocks the stem to wilt the top, and orders roots → tubes → leaves.

practice.prompt: Water first enters the plant through the…
practice.hint: Think about the part under the soil.
practice.explain: Roots take water in from the soil — that is the start of the path.

practice.prompt: Water travels up the stem through…
practice.hint: Look for pathways inside the stem.
practice.explain: Thin tubes (xylem) in the stem carry water upward.

practice.prompt: Block the stem. Leaves above the block…
practice.hint: The path is cut. What happens above a block?
practice.explain: A blocked stem stops water reaching leaves above the block.

practice.prompt: A stem has {a} open tubes and {b} blocked. Open tubes left?
practice.hint: Subtract the blocked tubes from the open ones.
practice.explain: {a} open minus {b} blocked leaves {=a-b} open tubes.

practice.prompt: Water climbed {a} cm, then {b} cm more. Total climb?
practice.hint: Add the two climbs along the stem.
practice.explain: Water climbed {a} + {b} = {=a+b} cm up the stem.

pool.explain: Water enters at roots, rises in stem tubes, reaches leaves.

choices: Leaves drink soil with no stem path
pool.explain: Leaves receive water via the stem; they do not drink soil alone.
Tubes transport water; leaves make food; flowers help seeds.

pool.hint: The pathway is broken at the crush.
pool.explain: Above a crush or block, water cannot continue upward.

pool.hint: Something must connect roots to leaves.
pool.explain: A clear stem pathway carries water from roots to leaves.

pool.prompt: A plant has {a} open stem tubes. {b} get crushed. How many still carry water?
pool.hint: Subtract crushed tubes from the open ones that can still carry water.
pool.explain: {a} open minus {b} crushed leaves {=a-b} working tubes.

items: cut stem to see coloured tubes
pool.hint: Set up, wait, then look inside.
pool.explain: Dye marks the tubes that carried water up the stem.

pool.prompt: Of {a} leaves above a block, all dry. How many dry?
pool.hint: Every leaf above a blocked stem loses the water path.
pool.explain: All {a} leaves above the block dry out.
